Never writes a body received with an unexpected Content-Encoding
'redirects' and 'framing' corpus categories pass
Zero silent corruption across the S1 corpus subset
Crash injection at every write boundary yields a byte-correct file after resume
Journal replay never panics under proptest truncation and bit-flip
Interval map property tests pass over 10000 generated operation sequences
Resume refuses on a changed strong validator and never splices
disk-full-at-97pct leaves a resumable state with no truncation
The final rename happens only after full verification
Zero silent corruption across the whole corpus so far
N connections give measurably higher throughput on an uncapped server
No overlapping writes under worker-death and interleaving-fuzz scenarios
Connections are reused after a segment completes, verified by handshake count
Falls back cleanly to a single stream when range support is absent

stages.name: Adaptive concurrency and ETA-aware work stealing

exit_criteria.text: The controller settles at or below the true optimum on every capped scenario
Never slower than a single connection would have been
ETA splitting measurably beats naive halving on the slow-worker scenario
Back-off honours Retry-After exactly with no self-inflicted rate limiting
dp explain output is sufficient to diagnose a bad decision from the log alone
Zero silent corruption
Matches or beats the HTTP/1.1 path on an h2 origin with one handshake instead of N
Detects a per-connection bandwidth cap and escalates to a second connection
Never exceeds the advertised SETTINGS_MAX_CONCURRENT_STREAMS
Flow-control tuning demonstrably improves throughput on a high-BDP path, documented before and after
Downloads correctly over HTTP/3 against the corpus server
Falls back within H3_RACE_TIMEOUT when UDP is blocked or throttled
Beats HTTP/2 on the slow-lossy benchmark condition
Disabling the h3 feature flag removes it entirely with zero effect on the scheduler
Capture works on current Chrome, Edge and Firefox
A download that fails with a bare URL succeeds with captured context
The native host rejects every malformed frame in the fuzz corpus without crash or over-allocation
Cookies never reach SQLite or any log
Default capture rules do not break ordinary browsing, verified on a manual site list
An expired signed URL is refreshed and the transfer continues from existing bytes
The compatibility check refuses an incompatible representation every time
Proxy corpus cases pass including proxies that break range support
Credentials live in the keyring; a trace-level log grep finds nothing
NTLM/Kerberos either supported or documented as a limitation with an ADR on the curl contingency
Non-DRM HLS and DASH assemble byte-identically to a reference ffmpeg run
Every DRM and live case is rejected, with a test asserting the rejection
Adversarial segment completion orders produce identical output
Works without FFmpeg for single-container cases and reports clearly when FFmpeg is required

adr_index.title: GUI toolkit choice deferred to Stage 10
Daemon-first architecture with a public IPC contract
Append-only journal for progress, SQLite for metadata
HTTP backends behind a TransferProtocol trait
The compatibility corpus is the primary asset
No DRM circumvention, no TLS interception
Adaptive concurrency instead of a fixed connection count

risks.text: Scope sprawl: the project fails by growing sideways rather than by being technically hard
risks.mitigation: Stage gates as hard walls; backlog instead of implementation; non-goals listed explicitly in docs/00

risks.text: Silent corruption ships undetected because it is invisible in casual testing
risks.mitigation: Deterministic content generator gives ground truth per byte; crash injection at every write boundary; scorecard row 1 is a release blocker

risks.text: The Rust HTTP/3 stack stays experimental and cannot be shipped
risks.mitigation: TransferProtocol trait keeps h3 quarantined behind a feature flag; S6 may legitimately end with 'works, stays behind the flag'

risks.text: Browser extension store review rejects or delays the extension over native messaging and host permissions
risks.mitigation: Minimal permissions with written justification; no remote code; reproducible build from source; version skew handled by the IPC handshake

risks.text: Single-maintainer bandwidth: ten stages is a long road
risks.mitigation: Each stage produces something independently useful; the CLI is a shippable product from S3 onward

risks.text: AI agents produce plausible code that does not compose into a system
risks.mitigation: The harness: PROVE-before-BUILD, Gate A proof fields, Gate D corpus rule, machine-validated progress file

risks.text: The compatibility corpus is not maintained and the strategy quietly fails
risks.mitigation: Gate D is non-waivable: no fix lands without its case; corpus metrics tracked in this file

risks.text: Adaptive concurrency oscillates or underperforms a well-chosen fixed count
risks.mitigation: Dedicated simulation scenarios; ADR-0009 names the fallback (fixed count with learned per-origin defaults)

session_log.summary: Researched IDM's published segmentation, the 2026 Rust ecosystem, Claude Code plugin/skill/hook schemas and AGENTS.md. Wrote the full docs/ specification set, ADRs 0001-0009, the agent harness, this progress file with its schema and validator, .claude and .codex configuration, and the in-repo plugin marketplace. No product code written.
session_log.left_in_progress: S0-T4: the validator needs its first successful run. S0-T9 through S0-T12 (toolchain install, licence files, CI, git init) are the remaining S0 work.

session_log.summary: Completed the Codex agent surface: verified empirically that Codex 0.146 loads all 9 project skills via a repo marketplace at .agents/plugins/marketplace.json, and that plugin_hooks is REMOVED — so enforcement moved to .githooks/pre-commit, which is agent-agnostic. Added a sync script so both agents read one source with CI drift detection. Fixed doctor.sh to find cargo in non-interactive shells. Added LICENSE, SECURITY.md, CONTRIBUTING.md, CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md, CHANGELOG.md, .gitignore, .gitattributes, rust-toolchain.toml, justfile, GitLab CI, and a link checker. Rewrote README with badges and mermaid. Reconciled docs from GitHub to GitLab.
session_log.left_in_progress: S0 has one criterion left: S0-C5, the fresh-session orientation test. It is verified by the NEXT session reading CLAUDE.md then HARNESS.md then progress.json and correctly stating what to work on without being told.
